subject: Reserved capacity variance — ClearWave production latency & throughput escalation
messages:
From: Alex Chen <ops@clearwave.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: ClearWave Engineering <eng@clearwave.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Production throughput drop + latency spike — urgent

Mina,

We started seeing a sustained degradation in request throughput and a correlated latency spike on our reserved pool around 08:45 PT. Error rates climbed to ~6% for small-gen routes and 12% for streaming completions; p95 latency moved from ~280ms up to ~1.2s. This is impacting live checkout flows.

Attached is a short CSV with rolling 1m throughput by shard and a handful of log snippets. Can you confirm whether this is a ClearWave reservation issue vs a broader dedicated-pool saturation upstream? We have a spike in concurrent prefixes right now from a new internal batch job but that should be routed to burst capacity per our config — it doesn't appear to be.

We need an initial triage and expected ETA for mitigation. If you need any more logs or an immediate 1:1 call I can join.

Thanks,
Alex Chen
SRE Lead, ClearWave
ops@clearwave.com

Attachments:
- clearwave_throughput_snapshot_20261018.csv (csv)
- support_log_snippet.txt (txt)
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Alex Chen <ops@clearwave.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Oct 2026 09:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production throughput drop + latency spike — urgent

Folks — looping you in. Summary: ClearWave (DW-7831) reports sustained reserved-capacity throughput deficit and latency/error increase starting ~08:45 PT. They attached a snapshot (see Alex) showing concentrated pressure on shard-3 and kvcache misses increasing during the window.

Immediate asks:
- Marissa: can you confirm whether reserved pool autoscaler recorded any failures to scale or allocation denials for the ClearWave reservation? Check allocation events 08:30–09:00 PT.
- Priyom: can we validate if smart-routing mistakenly sent the batch traffic to shared pools instead of burst capacity? Any recent routing policy changes?
- Aditya: please examine the serving runtime logs for shard-3 for elevated OOMs, kernel stalls, or queueing (08:30–09:10). Include GPU utilization and host-level metrics.

I will open an ops bridge if we see cross-customer impact. Alex — thanks for the packet; I will update within 30 minutes.

Mina Haddad
Senior Customer Reliability Manager | Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Alex Chen <ops@clearwave.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Oct 2026 09:41:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production throughput drop + latency spike — urgent

Verified: no autoscaler rejections in the reserved pool for ClearWave between 08:00–09:30 PT. Capacity delta shows reserved pool at 92% effective utilization with a short-lived spike to 99% at 08:46. We did see 15s delay on allocation of burst instances because a node group was undergoing rolling maintenance (control-plane scheduled). That cluster should have had maintenance drained, but the drain overlapped the spike window.

I am sharing a quick extract of allocation events in the bridge. Short term: we can force-add burst nodes for ClearWave if ops approves; there is a small risk to other tenants if we don't respect placement constraints.

-Marissa
Director, Dedicated Capacity Operations
Attachment: capacity_runbook_v2.pdf (pdf)
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Alex Chen <ops@clearwave.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Oct 2026 10:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production throughput drop + latency spike — urgent

Quick root-cause hypothesis from runtime traces: during the brief surge, smart-routing evaluated route stability and erroneously treated the new concurrent prefixes as \"unknown long tail\" and attempted to fall back to a compatible quantized variant hosted on shared nodes instead of the ClearWave-reserved burst path. That caused cross-pool traffic and KV cache churn — leading to higher p95 and elevated error retries.

Action plan (immediate):
- Toggle routing override for ClearWave to prefer reservation binding for 30m (Priyom) — done at 10:06 PT.
- Force-start two burst nodes from the dedicated burst node group (Marissa) — pending approval; expected online by 10:18 PT.
- Apply temporary cache pinning to keep key prefixes hot on reserved hosts (Aditya) — in progress.

I will escalate to Stephanie/Evelyn if we see any service-level correlation to other reserved customers.

-Priyom
Senior Product Manager, Routing & Orchestration
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Chen <ops@clearwave.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 15:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production throughput drop + latency spike — urgent

Update and executive note for follow-up:

Summary: ClearWave's production issue on 10/18 was caused by an interaction between smart-routing's classification of an emergent batch prefix and an overlapping control-plane maintenance window that delayed burst node allocation. The immediate mitigations (routing override + forced burst nodes + KV cache pinning) restored throughput to baseline by ~10:25 PT and reduced errors to <0.5% within 40 minutes.

Impact: brief SLA exposure for ClearWave (p95 breach ~40 minutes). No other dedicated customers flagged similar degradation.

Actions taken:
- Remediated the customer in 40 minutes with a manual override and burst node injection.
- Logged a routing policy regression and created a tracker to avoid treat-as-long-tail misclassification for pinned reservations.
- Added a control-plane scheduling safeguard: block rolling maintenance on node groups with active reserved-burst throttles during business hours (Priyom & Marissa to own).
- Recommended we offer ClearWave a one-time service credit for the p95 window and an ops-run review; Stephanie please advise on credit/exec note.

Next steps / owners:
- Priyom: routing policy patch and regression test (ETA 2026-10-22).
- Marissa: update maintenance calendar enforcement and automation (ETA 2026-10-21).
- Aditya: produce a short playbook to pin KV hot sets for reserved customers when burst fallback occurs (ETA 2026-10-20).
- Stephanie: determine customer compensation and whether to escalate to CRO for approval (ETA EOD 2026-10-19).

Alex — thanks for rapid reports and the initial CSV. I'll follow up with a short incident summary and the slides for exec brief if needed.

Mina Haddad
Senior Customer Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 415-555-0139
